assertions: The news/report is false — it is not true
The King has not taken Cambridge; Cambridge has not fallen into the King's hands and remains with the Parliament side
The King's side is weak and declining: lord of the 7th entering his fall and afflicted, with Mars afflicting the cusp of the 7th and Saturn vitiating the cusp of the 10th
The querent/Parliament side is the stronger: lady of the Ascendant in her exaltation, with the Sun on the cusp of the Ascendant
The rumour will prove groundless and come to nothing, signified by the Moon cadent in a sign wherein she nothing delights and all angles moveable
method: Lilly horary astrology — Christian Astrology Book II, judgment of rumours/news truth and war opponent (Asc = querent/Parliament, 7th = King as opponent)
reasoning: All angles moveable = unstable, unsettled news. Moon, co-significatrix of the report, cadent and in a sign wherein she nothing delights = weak/peregrine, rumour lacks substance and will vanish. Lady of Ascendant in exaltation = Parliament/querent side essentially dignified and superior. Lord of 7th entering his fall and afflicted = King's side falling and unable to effect the reported taking. Saturn vitiating 10th cusp and Mars afflicting 7th cusp further afflict the King's honour/power and party, while Sun on Ascendant cusp strengthens the querent side. Hence the proposition is negated.
summary: The report is false — the King has not taken Cambridge.
